text:
miriam-sre: Heads-up — we're seeing an ECC correctable spike in us-west-2 GPU pool 3, started ~10m ago. ~60% of cards reporting >10 correctables/min.
alex_infra: I see it, metrics show an Xid flood on a handful of hosts but mostly correctables. No uncorrectables yet.
carlos-ops: Noted. Capacity in us-west-2 is pretty tight today (Dedicated reservations + a batch job). If we start draining we may hit capacity alarms.
miriam-sre: Proposal: apply soft-drain (no new allocations, finish inflight, lighter eviction) for hosts that exceed 15 correctables/min sustained for 5m. Hard drain only if we get >1 Xid or any uncorrectable. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
alex_infra: Agree with soft-drain thresholds. Add an extra rule: if 3 hosts in the same rack hit soft-drain within 15m, escalate to cluster-level rampdown and shift routing to other AZs.
jen-oncall: Can we enrich the signal before action? e.g., check thermal/power anomalies and nvml counters so we don't drain for telemetry noise. I can patch the enrichment step in the pipeline.
priya-mlops: We also have the ML classifier prototype that predicts card failure windows from correctable patterns+thermal. It flagged 2 hosts with >0.8 probability of failure within 24h. Could use that as a stronger signal to progress from soft->hard drain.
miriam-sre: Nice — combine heuristics: metric thresholds -> enrichment checks -> ML score. If ML score >0.75 and correctables >25/min -> auto-hard-drain. Otherwise soft-drain.
deploy-bot: deploy job redb-signal-enrichment v1.3 started by jen-oncall at 1937623510
alex_infra: Adding a short operator playbook snippet for the soft-drain command:

```
# soft-drain host
redwoodctl node cordon hgpu-12 --mode=soft --grace-period=300
redwoodctl node inspect hgpu-12 --nvml --last-24h
```

miriam-sre: We'll also add a temporary routing policy: reduce batch size and lower max-inflight per-connection for affected hosts to reduce stress while draining. That should help latency-sensitive routes.
carlos-ops: Cost/regional tradeoff: if we shift traffic to other AZs we may trigger cross-AZ egress and bump up cost. For now prefer cross-region only if SLA-critical.
jen-oncall: I'm going to run the soft-drain on the top 4 hosts that match the threshold and start enrichment. Patch applied.
priya-mlops: I'll hook ML scores into the alert note so oncall sees predicted risk + recommended action.
miriam-sre: Runbook update: add a "surgery mode" flag for high-impact pools — surgery mode = aggressive soft-drain + reduced batch sizing + enable ML-based hard-drain after 2h if persistent. Keep manual approval window for Dedicated customer pools.
alex_infra: Also adding circuit-breaker: if correctable rate falls but Xid spikes appear, immediately escalate to eng-oncall and consider emergency host replacement.
jen-oncall: Soft-drain complete on hgpu-12,hgpu-14,hgpu-21,hgpu-22 at 1937623585. Monitoring. :thumbsup:
miriam-sre: Good. We'll review telemetry at +15m and +30m. If cluster error rate doesn't drop by 50% we start replacement rotation and a ticket to HW team.
priya-mlops: Kicking off model scoring on those hosts now. Should have scores in ~4m.
alex_infra: Quick note — avoid auto-hard-drain for Dedicated pools unless explicit opt-in from account owner. Put that in playbook.
miriam-sre: Agreed. Adding consent check.
jen-oncall: Filing a short post-incident note template while it's fresh so we capture thresholds chosen and who approved the surgery mode.
carlos-ops: If we need capacity fast, can we temporarily relax some batch caching to free RAM on affected hosts? Might reduce performance but buys time.
miriam-sre: Ok plan: enrichment + ML scoring -> soft-drain now -> review at +15/+30 -> if ML>0.75 & persistent -> hard-drain (except Dedicated without consent). I'll update the ticket and runbook. Thanks all.
